before.title: ATTESA E-TS Hydraulic Pump and Nitrogen Accumulator Failure
before.description: The GT-R's (and GTS-4's) ATTESA E-TS all-wheel-drive system uses an electric hydraulic pump and a nitrogen-charged accumulator mounted near the fuel tank to pressurize the front-drive transfer clutch. With age the accumulator loses its nitrogen pre-charge and the pump and pressure switch wear out, so the system can no longer hold pressure; the car drops to rear-drive only and the 4WD warning light comes on (often logging fault code 18 for low accumulator pressure). The accumulator cannot be recharged, and an ABS fault will also trigger the ATTESA light because the systems are linked.
before.solution: Replace the accumulator (Nissan part 41630-20U00, shared across R32-R34 GT-R) and bleed the system; replace or rebuild the pump if it no longer primes. Always check ATTESA fluid level in the trunk-mounted reservoir and pull fault codes before replacing parts.
symptoms: 4WD warning light on the cluster
ATTESA pump runs much longer than normal at startup
Repeated clicking from the ATTESA relay in the trunk
Front wheels never receive torque / no AWD engagement
Jerky or surging AWD engagement as pressure cycles

before.title: Ceramic Turbocharger Exhaust Wheel Failure
before.description: Factory twin turbos on the GT-R (and the single turbos on RB20DET/RB25DET GTS-T models) use lightweight ceramic exhaust wheels for fast spool, but the brittle ceramic shears off the shaft with age, heat cycles, detonation, rev-limiter hits, or boost much above the stock ~0.9-1.1 bar. A failed wheel kills boost instantly, dumps shards into the exhaust, and can take the turbo's bearings and seals with it, with documented cases of consequential engine damage. Only N1 and Nür special editions came with steel exhaust wheels from the factory.
before.solution: Keep boost at or below roughly 0.9-1.0 bar on original ceramic turbos, and replace failed or tired units with steel-wheel rebuilds or aftermarket steel-wheel turbos (N1, Garrett, HKS, Tomei) before raising boost. Inspect for shaft play and smoke whenever turbo health is in doubt.
symptoms: Sudden loss of boost and power
Loud metallic rattle or whoosh from the turbo
Heavy smoke from the exhaust
Ceramic fragments found in downpipe or cat
Excessive turbine shaft play on inspection

before.title: Crank Angle Sensor (CAS) Failure: Hot Stalling and No-Start
before.description: The optical crank angle sensor driven off the exhaust camshaft on RB20/RB25/RB26 engines degrades with age and heat, causing intermittent loss of timing signal. The classic pattern is an engine that runs fine cold, then cuts out, backfires or stalls as it heats up and refuses to restart until it cools; a fully dead CAS gives crank-but-no-start. The sensor's half-moon alignment drive pin can also break if the CAS is installed incorrectly, producing popping, backfiring and no-start after reinstallation.
before.solution: Replace the CAS with a new OEM unit (Nissan 23731-5L30A supersession fits RB20/RB25/RB26) and verify base timing afterward; confirm the half-moon drive pin is intact whenever the sensor is removed. Carry-out testing first, since ignition-harness faults can mimic CAS symptoms.
symptoms: Engine stalls when hot, restarts only after cooling down
Crank but no start
Sudden RPM drop with backfire
Misfires and rough idle that worsen with heat
Loud backfire after extended cranking

before.title: Ignition Coil Pack and Engine-Valley Harness Degradation (Misfire Under Boost)
before.description: The six individual coil packs and their harness sit in the hot valley between the cam covers on RB20/RB25/RB26 engines, where decades of heat cycles crack coil boots, embrittle the harness insulation and corrode crimped terminals. The classic result is a misfire that appears only under boost or load, often accompanied by an audible click as spark arcs to ground through cracked boots; arcing leaves small bubbled marks on the underside of the coil packs. Failing igniter packs (separate module on RB20/RB26) produce similar symptoms.
before.solution: Test coils for 0.6-0.9 ohm primary resistance, inspect for arcing marks, and replace the set with OEM or quality aftermarket coils (Splitfire, R35-coil conversion kits) along with fresh plugs gapped to spec. Repair or replace the crispy valley sub-harness at the same time, since the harness is the culprit at least as often as the coils.
symptoms: Misfire or breakup only under boost/load
Rough idle and hesitation
Audible clicking from the engine valley as spark arcs
Misfire worsens as the engine heats up
Bubbled arc marks on the underside of coil packs

before.title: R34 GT-R Getrag V160 6-Speed Synchro Wear and Gear Grind
before.description: The R34 GT-R's Getrag V160 6-speed has strong hard parts but notoriously weak synchros, with 3rd gear (and then 2nd) typically grinding first, eventually refusing clean engagement; AWD traction puts extra shock load through the box and accelerates the wear. Nissan officially treats the V160 as non-serviceable (replace only), replacement boxes are scarce and very expensive, and a correct rebuild requires one of only a handful of specialists. Earlier R32/R33 5-speeds also crunch 2nd/3rd synchros with age, but parts for those are far cheaper and more available.
before.solution: Address grinding early with a specialist Getrag rebuild using updated synchros or aftermarket engagement-ring upgrades, before damaged synchros chew the gears themselves. Use proper Getrag-spec gear oil and avoid fast cold shifts to extend synchro life.
symptoms: Grinding or crunching into 3rd gear, especially when cold
Crunch into 2nd on quick shifts
Gear refuses to engage at higher RPM
Notchy, baulky shift action that worsens over time

before.title: RB26DETT Oil Pump Drive Collar Failure (Narrow Crank Snout)
before.description: Early R32 GT-R crankshafts (built from 1989 until the design was revised in late 1992/early 1993) have a narrow oil pump drive collar with excessive clearance to the pump's inner gear. At sustained high RPM or when bouncing off the rev limiter, harmonic vibration hammers the drive against the pump gear until the gear shatters, causing instant loss of oil pressure and, in many documented cases, complete engine seizure requiring a full rebuild. Even later RB26 cranks benefit from the fix when the engine is used hard.
before.solution: During any engine-out work, have the crank snout machined and a press-fit extended crank collar (Reimax, Tomei, JUN style) installed, ideally paired with an N1 or aftermarket oil pump. The N1 pump alone does NOT fix the root cause, which is the crank drive, not the pump.
symptoms: Low or fluctuating oil pressure at idle
Sudden drop of oil pressure to zero at high RPM
Loud knocking immediately after hard revving
Metallic debris in oil or oil filter
Engine seizure after rev-limiter abuse

before.title: Structural Rust: Strut Towers, Rear Arches, Sills and Boot Floor
before.description: All three Skyline generations are now 24-37 years old and were built with minimal rustproofing, so corrosion in the front strut tower seams, rear wheel arches, sills, boot floor and chassis rails is the single biggest body concern on imports. Water gets past aging boot seals and stone chips in the rear arches trap moisture, while strut-top corrosion can bulge the towers and become a structural and alignment problem. Freshly blacked-out undersides on cars for sale are a documented red flag for hidden rust repair.
before.solution: Inspect strut tower seams, inner rear arches, sills, jacking points and boot floor before purchase, and cut out and weld in new metal at the first sign of bubbling; strut tower repairs run roughly $650-850 per side and full multi-area repairs can reach several thousand dollars. Cavity-wax and underseal sound cars to stop it starting.
symptoms: Bubbling paint along engine-bay strut tower seams
Blistering on rear wheel arch lips
Damp carpet or standing water in the boot
Crusty sills and crushed/rusted jacking points
Fresh black underseal hiding the underbody

before.title: Super HICAS Rear-Steer System Aging: Leaks, Solenoid Faults and Worn Ball Joints
before.description: All performance Skylines of this era carry HICAS/Super HICAS four-wheel steering (hydraulic on R32, electric rack on R33/R34), and with age the rear rack seals leak, solenoids and the rear-toe control hardware fail, and the system's rear ball joints wear and introduce vague, wandering rear-end feel. Aftermarket steering wheels on a non-HICAS-compatible boss confuse the steering-angle sensor and set faults. The system is so commonly problematic that deleting it with a lock-bar kit is the accepted community fix, though a botched delete can light the 4WD/ABS warning lamps.
before.solution: Run the HICAS self-diagnosis to confirm the fault, then either repair the leaking rack/solenoids and worn ball joints or fit a quality HICAS delete (lock bar plus looped or capped hydraulic lines on R32) - the route most owners choose. Ensure ground wires and the steering-angle sensor are handled correctly to avoid warning lights.
symptoms: HICAS warning light on the dash
Vague, wandering or 'rear-steering itself' feel at speed
Hydraulic fluid leaking from the rear rack (R32)
Clunks from worn rear HICAS ball joints
Uneven rear tire wear
